steps: An object is in motion if its position changes with time with respect to a reference point.
A passenger sitting in a moving bus is at rest with respect to the bus but in motion with respect to a tree outside.
Think: is the passenger moving or at rest?
Distance is the total length of the path travelled, and it is a vector quantity.
Displacement is the shortest straight line from start to end, with a direction.
Think: what is the displacement after one full lap?

lessons.flaw: says displacement after a full lap equals the track length
steps: If a runner completes one full lap of a circular track, the displacement is the length of the track.
Distance is the total length of the path travelled.
Think: where does the runner end up?
Distance is the total length of the path travelled and is a scalar quantity.
Displacement is the shortest straight line from the starting point to the final point, with a direction.
Think: which of the two can be zero after a full lap?
Speed is the distance travelled in one unit of time. Its SI unit is metre per second.
Average speed is total distance divided by total time taken.
Think: how would you find the average speed of a trip?
Speed is distance per unit time and it has both magnitude and direction.
Velocity is displacement per unit time.
Think: which one needs a direction?
Speed is distance per unit time, and its SI unit is kilometre per hour.
Average speed is total distance divided by total time.
Think: what unit would you use in a lab?

lessons.flaw: says two cars with equal speed must have equal velocity
steps: Two cars with the same speed always have the same velocity.
Velocity is displacement per unit time and has direction.
Think: what if they drive in opposite directions?
Velocity is displacement in one unit of time, so it has magnitude and direction.
A car moving at 60 km/h towards the north has a velocity of 60 km/h north.
Think: how is this different from speed?
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time, measured in metre per second squared.
If velocity increases by 10 m/s in 5 s, the acceleration is 2 m/s^2.
Think: what if the velocity does not change?
Acceleration is the change in velocity divided by the time taken.
If velocity increases by 10 m/s in 5 s, the acceleration is 50 m/s^2.
Think: divide or multiply?
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time.
An object moving with a constant velocity has a large constant acceleration.
Think: does the velocity change here?
When the velocity of an object decreases with time, the acceleration is negative and is called retardation.
An object moving with constant velocity has zero acceleration.
Think: can an object slow down and still have acceleration?
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time.
The SI unit of acceleration is metre per second squared (m/s^2).
Think: how is this unit different from the unit of speed?
In a distance-time graph, time is on the horizontal axis and distance on the vertical axis.
The slope of a distance-time graph gives the speed of the object.
Think: what does a steeper line mean?
The slope of a distance-time graph gives the speed.
A horizontal line in a distance-time graph shows that the object moves at constant speed.
Think: what is the slope of a horizontal line?

lessons.flaw: area under v-t graph is acceleration
steps: In a velocity-time graph, a line parallel to the time axis shows constant velocity.
The area under a velocity-time graph gives the acceleration of the object.
Think: what has units of metres?

lessons.flaw: slope of distance-time graph is acceleration
steps: In a distance-time graph, a straight line sloping upwards shows constant speed.
The slope of a distance-time graph gives the acceleration of the object.
Think: what is distance divided by time?
In a velocity-time graph, a straight line sloping upwards shows uniform acceleration.
The area under a velocity-time graph gives the displacement of the object.
Think: what does a line parallel to the time axis show?
Speed is a scalar quantity because it has magnitude only.
Velocity is a vector quantity because it has direction as well.
Think: which of these two changes when a car turns a corner at steady speed?
